output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows 37 confirmed incidents in September and 36 in October, in line with the roughly 38 a month before. Of those, 47 were later moved by the Brackwater integration account into the "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" category. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the 4-hour containment warning flag, and none of the 47 had a containment timestamp. Moved cases drop out of the incident count and the containment SLA figures, which is why the report shows 100% containment and a fall in incidents. A Tessaline advisory describes a connector bug (we run 4.1.7) that overwrites categories after that warning fires, and the timing fits. I can't yet tell whether this is a bug or deliberate. I'm about 65% confident it is the bug. Either way the numbers are unreliable. Do not cut the Halvard retainer, and do not approve the 60k bonus yet. Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents and have your team and Halvard check that each was contained. Remove category-edit rights from the integration role, and upgrade the connector or remove the category field from its sync. Ask Brackwater to explain in writing. Check the API gateway logs to see whether the connector made the changes. Hold the service credits until you know the cause.
